Cell morphology and chaining analysis via microscopy

Data & Platforms: Vibrio fischeri envC nlpD double mutant
Application Areas: Bacterial Interbacterial Competition and Defense Mechanisms
Key Research Thinking Patterns: Genetic Suppression and Functional Rescue: Utilizing suppressor mutant isolation and sequencing to identify compensatory pathways that restore fitness in division-defective or stress-sensitive mutants (e.g., isolating VF_1477 suppressors in amiB mutants to elucidate cell division mechanics).

Host-Mediated Competitive Exclusion: Employing in vivo competitive colonization assays in the Euprymna scolopes squid model to demonstrate how specific bacterial effectors, such as the TasL lipoprotein, drive the targeted elimination of competitors to shape microbiome spatial structure.

Comparative Phylogenomics and Structural Modeling: Integrating metagenomic datasets (Sargasso Sea) with homology modeling (RaptorX) and domain analysis (Pfam) to trace the evolutionary history and structural conservation of respiratory enzymes like alternative oxidases across diverse bacterial lineages.

Metabolic-Physiological Coupling: Linking redox state and metabolic profiling (NADH/NAD+ ratios, ROS detection) with phenotypic outcomes (biofilm formation, motility) to define how nitric oxide detoxification and peptidoglycan recycling jointly regulate bacterial survival in host niches.
Summary Description: Anne K. Dunn specializes in bacterial physiology and symbiosis, focusing on how metabolic regulation and interbacterial competition drive microbiome assembly in marine environments. Using Vibrio fischeri and the Euprymna scolopes model, she elucidates mechanisms of cell division, biofilm architecture, and Type VI secretion system-mediated competition. Her work integrates genetic suppression strategies, in vivo colonization assays, and comparative phylogenomics to reveal how respiratory flexibility and cell wall remodeling govern bacterial fitness. By connecting molecular mechanisms of stress response and adhesion to macro-level ecological outcomes, her research provides a comprehensive framework for understanding the evolutionary and physiological determinants of successful host-microbe interactions.
